files.decision: Preserve the complete upstream MIT notice.
Maintain original English documentation for this JavaScript adaptation.
Review tooling versions and Foundry types; keep JavaScript tooling and the local lockfile.
Adapt the ES module build while omitting TypeScript-only path aliases and retaining the unified src layout and per-id output.
Retain Rui Pinheiro's MIT attribution and review the deliberately limited JavaScript fallback.
Use explicit stable/prerelease publication, validate the selected commit, create its associated tag, and publish verified assets with curated release notes.
Intentionally omitted: no Discord announcements or Foundry website publication.
Keep a small entry point that imports styles and installs the lifecycle listeners.
Register JavaScript lifecycle modules centrally, including the local ready phase.
Register settings, Handlebars helpers, and the public module API during init.
Keep setup integration explicit; the demonstration does not wrap unrelated core functionality by default.
Track upstream HMR changes for review; the local implementation promises rebuilding and documented reloads, not full parity.
Keep named settings registration and access in one JavaScript module.
Keep module-prefixed logging with local diagnostics behavior.
Register namespaced template helpers to avoid collisions.
Derive the module id from src/module.json instead of a TypeScript static alias.
The upstream file contains only TypeScript interfaces; the local file is an independent runtime API, not a port of type aliases.
Keep one source manifest and lang paths; generate release URLs and leave verified unset until real runtime tests.
Preserve live packs while cleaning only a marked per-id output directory.
Link the per-id output to Foundry; refuse replacing an existing real directory.
Rename explicit project fields and namespaces without rewriting upstream provenance or unrelated files.
Compile declared packs from packs-src and require explicit overwrite of existing output.
Extract compiled packs into tracked source directories with explicit overwrite handling.
Resolve declared pack names and paths for the local source/output layout.
Start an explicitly configured local Foundry installation using the chosen version.
Document local Foundry Data and versioned installation paths without committing personal configuration.

intentionalDifferences: JavaScript source, JavaScript build helpers, and JSDoc rather than TypeScript compilation.
src/module.json, src/module.js, src/lang, src/styles, src/templates, src/assets, and src/scripts.
A built module lives inside dist/<module-id>; the release ZIP preserves that directory.
Release assets are named module.json and module.zip.
Download URLs are pinned to the exact tag; stable manifests use the latest stable feed and prerelease manifests remain pinned to their own tags.
Independent Node-based ZIP packaging and verification.

No Git-history-derived release notes, pull-request workflows, scheduled checks, upstream bots, automatic merges, or Discord/Foundry website publication; release changes come from curated CHANGELOG entries.
Development uses rebuilding and documented reloads; it does not promise parity with every upstream HMR behavior.
